name: range_day_band_fade_003
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, range-bound sessions (ADX < 20, flat 5-minute VWAP slope) create a microstructure where VWAP-benchmarked institutional algorithms aggressively defend prices that deviate 0.05-0.10% from session VWAP — they treat every tick away from benchmark as a free fill opportunity and immediately place opposing limit orders. When 1-minute MFI simultaneously reaches extreme (≤22 or ≥78), it confirms that short-term buying or selling pressure has exhausted available counterparty interest, leaving only the VWAP algos on one side of the book. The 20-minute Bollinger band acts as a safety filter: if price has already pierced the band, the move is a regime break rather than an overreaction, and the fade is skipped. At 5-second resolution we enter the moment MFI exhaustion prints with a bullish/bearish close bar, capturing 5-8 option points of the first-leg VWAP reversion before the next directional impulse.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Cumulative from session open — no lookback needed. NIFTY's session VWAP is the primary institutional benchmark; every TWAP/VWAP algo executes relative to this level.

indicators.name: adx_120
indicators.purpose: ADX over 120 bars = 10 minutes. Original used ADX(14) on 1-min = 14-minute ADX as a CONTEXT FILTER — detecting range vs trend regime. We use the same 10-minute window (not 12x blind scaling) because this is about detecting the intraday regime of the current session, not the trade trigger itself. Warmup requires 2× period = 240 bars.

indicators.name: bb_upper_240
indicators.purpose: Bollinger upper band over 240 bars = 20 minutes. Same TIME window as the original (20 × 1-min = 20 min). The BB is a safety filter: if NIFTY price is OUTSIDE the 20-min band, the move is a genuine breakout, not overreaction. We only fade moves that are inside the band (i.e., normal range-day oscillation).

indicators.name: bb_lower_240
indicators.purpose: Bollinger lower band — same rationale as bb_upper_240.

indicators.name: vwap_slope_60
indicators.purpose: VWAP slope over 60 bars = 5 minutes, normalized by 20-bar ATR. Original used 10-bar slope on 1-min = 10 min; we compress to 5 min because we need the VWAP to be flat NOW (short-term flat), not just over a longer window. A flat 5-min VWAP confirms the range structure persists into the current bar.

indicators.name: mfi_12
indicators.purpose: MFI over 12 bars = 1 minute. Original used MFI(5) on 1-min = 5 minutes. Compressed to 1 minute because at 5-second resolution we are looking for FAST exhaustion — a climax print in 12 bars (1 minute) means the short-term pressure just peaked. A 5-minute MFI would be a lagging signal by the time exhaustion resolves, missing the entry window.

conditions: (close - vwap) / vwap <= -vwap_dev_threshold (default -0.0005, i.e. ~11 pts below VWAP on NIFTY 23000)
close > bb_lower_240 (not a breakdown, just a range-day dip)
close > open (bullish close bar confirms start of reversion)
buy_ce.confirmation: Bullish close bar (close > open) confirming the first-tick reversion from oversold extreme

conditions: (close - vwap) / vwap >= +vwap_dev_threshold (default +0.0005, i.e. ~11 pts above VWAP on NIFTY 23000)
close < bb_upper_240 (not a breakout, just range-day overshoot)
close < open (bearish close bar confirms start of fade)
buy_pe.confirmation: Bearish close bar (close < open) confirming the first-tick rejection from overbought extreme

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points adverse move. On a confirmed range day (ADX < 20), a move of >8 spot points in one direction from entry indicates the range structure is breaking into a trend; this is the thesis invalidation point and we exit before momentum algos compound the move further.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points towards VWAP. When NIFTY is 11-20 pts from VWAP on a range day, partial VWAP reversion of 14 pts captures 70-130% of the initial gap in the first 30-90 seconds — consistent with the 1-minute VWAP-algo accumulation pattern. This gives a 1:1.75 R:R at symmetric stop.

filters.vix_filter: none (VIX incorporated indirectly via ADX range-day check; original used VIX 12-24 but ADX is a cleaner range filter for 5s bars)
filters.time_filter: 10:15-14:15 IST only (avoid first hour noise and late-day trend ignition)
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY index volume is inherently high; volume filter replaced by MFI exhaustion signal which is volume-weighted
filters.trend_filter: ADX(120) < adx_threshold is the primary trend filter

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — regime dependent; works only on range days which occur 40-60% of sessions

adaptation_notes: Original was a cross-sectional nifty200 equity strategy. Converted to single-instrument NIFTY index. Key changes: (1) VWAP deviation threshold compressed from 0.7% (stocks can deviate this far) to 0.05% default (NIFTY index rarely deviates more than 0.3% on a range day); (2) MFI period compressed from 5-min to 1-min because we want FAST exhaustion at the entry bar not lagging confirmation; (3) ADX period recalibrated to 10-minute window (120 bars) maintaining same time duration as original 14-min ADX; (4) BB period kept at 20 minutes = 240 bars (same time window — this is a fixed-time filter, not a lookback-scaled one); (5) VWAP slope reduced from 10-min to 5-min window for tighter flatness requirement; (6) Hold time compressed from 5-22 min to 15-120 seconds; (7) No volume filter — replaced by MFI exhaustion which is inherently volume-weighted.
weaknesses: Range days that appear to be low-ADX at session start can break into trends intraday — ADX lags regime changes by 5-10 minutes.
NIFTY index VWAP deviation of 0.05% may generate too-frequent signals on days with continuous drift; vwap_slope filter is critical to avoid.
MFI(12) on 5-second NIFTY bars can be noisy due to index volume aggregation methodology.
Effective only on 40-60% of sessions (range days) — dead capital on trend days.

_source.original_stop: 0.45% from entry or 0.6 × atr_14 beyond signal extreme
_source.original_target: session VWAP or middle Bollinger band
